sentences.text: Agilisaurus louderbacki is the only species in this genus of ornithischian dinosaur, which lived in eastern Asia during the Middle Jurassic.
This animal reached a length of about 1.2 to 1.7 meters, stood 60 centimeters high at the hip, and had a mass near 40 kilograms.
Its teeth featured wavy enamel patterns once believed to be exclusive to duck-billed dinosaurs, indicating a high resistance to wear.
Measurements of its leg bones suggest it was a very rapid bipedal runner that balanced itself with a long tail.
The single known specimen, known as the holotype, was unearthed in 1984 while workers built the Zigong Dinosaur Museum.
In 1992, the discoverer named a second species, previously called Yandusaurus multidens, as Agilisaurus multidens because it shared traits with the first.
The creature ate plants using leaf-shaped teeth designed to crush abrasive food.
Researchers propose it might have lived underground since it lacked the bony supports usually found in dinosaur tails.
Later analysis shows the second species is more evolutionarily advanced than the original Agilisaurus.
Originally placed in the invalid family Fabrosauridae, it is now thought to sit near heterodontosaurs on the branch leading to Marginocephalia within Neornithischia.
Disagreement over the second species led to its reassignment in 2005 to the new genus Hexinlusaurus.
This genus inhabited the region between 170.9 and 154.8 million years ago, spanning the Bajocian to the Oxfordian stages.
